title: The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume
one_line: Stocks rise around their earnings announcements; buying expected announcers and shorting non-announcers earned > 60 bps/month (1972-2004), strongest where announcement volume (small-investor buying) is high.

findings.statement: Long expected announcers / short non-announcers: > 60 bps per month.
Larger for stocks with big predicted volume surges and small-investor buying.

reported_results.headline: Stocks rise around their earnings announcements; buying expected announcers and shorting non-announcers earned > 60 bps/month (1972-2004), strongest where announcement volume (small-investor buying) is high.

tradable_edge: Stock-level; index cousin is the earnings-cluster spec.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
